label: GO step, strongly committed to a2 after an unrewarded trial
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the policy strongly favours a2 (choice logit a1-a2 < about -4.4; all activity is in the bottom two choice bins, model_act == 2 always) and almost only when the previous trial was unrewarded (prev_reward == 0 holds 98.8% of mass; after rewarded trials it gives only tiny activations, which are most of the missed lowest-quartile steps). It is essentially a2-specific: there is no counterpart for a1. Uses only observed variables plus the agent own policy output; the upcoming action == 2 version scores lower (dev F1 0.70) because it includes weak a2 choices. Being in the previous rare-vs-common transition or state did not help. False positives are confident-a2 GO steps after no reward where the feature stays silent, often when unrewarded trials came in a row. Absent in the first ~10 episode trials and grows later in the episode. Activation is larger with a more negative choice logit (choice < -8 gives precision 0.80 and mass recall 0.90). Dev: P 0.75, R 0.86, F1 0.80, mass recall 0.985.

issues: The core claims hold. The feature fires only at GO (all activation mass; D1 and D2 have zero active steps). model_act is 2 for all of the mass. Only 60 active steps have choice in [-4.44, -1.52) and none are above that. prev_reward==0 holds 98.8% of the mass, and the same predicate with prev_reward==1 gets precision 0.057 and mass recall 0.012.

Systematic false-positive class: early-episode trials. The profile shows zero activations in trials 0-9 and a 0.005 rate in trials 10-19. The predicate restricted to ep_trial<20 has 8898 predicted steps at precision 0.067, which is roughly half of all false positives. The explanation mentions that the feature is 'absent in the first ~10 trials' but the predicate ignores this, and the silent window actually runs to about trial 20.

Adding (ep_trial>=20) alone lifts dev precision from 0.75 to 0.876 and F1 from 0.80 to 0.861, with mass recall unchanged (0.984). So the original sub-0.8 test F1 comes from a missing condition, not from scattered noise.

Small extra gap: after an a1 trial the predicate's cases almost never fire (prev_action==1: 525 predicted steps, precision 0.06). So the feature tracks continuing a2 after no reward, not switching to a2.

The explanation attributes the false positives to runs of several unrewarded trials. That is only partly true: precision is 0.62 when the trial before was also unrewarded vs 0.79 when it was rewarded. The main false-positive driver is episode position (trials 0-19), which the explanation does not identify as the false-positive source.
uses_future=false is correct: the predicate uses only prev_reward (observed) and the policy logit.
